facts.statement: Chungkingosaurus is a stegosaurian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Upper Shaximiao Formation in modern-day China.
facts.quote: Chungkingosaurus (meaning "Chongqing Lizard") is a genus of stegosaurian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic Upper Shaximiao Formation in what is now China.

facts.statement: Chungkingosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic Oxfordian stage, approximately 156 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 156 millones de años, en el Oxfordiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The holotype of Chungkingosaurus jiangbeiensis was one of the smallest stegosaurs, measuring less than four meters in length despite being an adult.
facts.quote: According to Dong e.a. the Chungkingosaurus jiangbeiensis holotype was one of the smallest stegosaurs with a length of less than four metres, even though it was apparently an adult, judging by the ossification of the sacrum.

facts.statement: Chungkingosaurus jiangbeiensis measured approximately 4.00 meters in length, 1.80 meters in height, and weighed about 1 tonne.
facts.quote: llegando a medir 4,00 metros de largo, 1,80 de alto y con un peso de 1 tonelada

facts.statement: A skeleton model in the Chongqing Municipal museum depicts Chungkingosaurus with fourteen pairs of plates and two pairs of tail spikes.
facts.quote: A skeleton model in the Chongqing Municipal museum shows fourteen pairs of plates. This model also has two pairs of tail spikes.

facts.statement: Chungkingosaurus had fourteen pairs of plates on its back that transformed into spikes towards the tail.
facts.quote: En el dorso tenía 14 pares de placas que se transformaban en púas hacia la cola.

facts.statement: The tail of Chungkingosaurus appears to show at least five spikes, suggesting more than the traditional two pairs found on the limb.
facts.quote: La cola parece mostrar por lo menos un total de cinco espinas, sugiriendo más que los dos pares tradicionales en la extremidad.

facts.statement: Chungkingosaurus was quadrupedal but could rear up on its hind legs to eat leaves from higher branches of trees.
facts.quote: Era cuadrúpedo, pero podía reincorporarse sobre sus patas traseras y comer de las hojas más altas de los árboles.

facts.statement: Chungkingosaurus was a herbivore, like all stegosaurs.
facts.quote: Like all stegosaurs, Chungkingosaurus was a herbivore.

facts.statement: Chungkingosaurus is considered part of the family Stegosauridae.
facts.quote: Chungkingosaurus es considerado parte de la familia Stegosauridae.

facts.statement: In 2008, Maidment and colleagues assigned Chungkingosaurus to the family Huayangosauridae.
facts.quote: In 2008 Maidment e.a. assigned it to the Huayangosauridae.

facts.statement: The form of its dermal armor makes Chungkingosaurus considered a relative of Kentrosaurus and Dacentrurus in the subfamily Kentrosaurinae.
facts.quote: La forma de la armadura dérmica hace que sea considerado pariente de Kentrosaurus y de Dacentrurus en la subfamilia Kentrosaurinae.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul suggested in 2010 that Chungkingosaurus was the juvenile form of Tuojiangosaurus.
facts.quote: However, Gregory S. Paul in 2010 suggested that Chungkingosaurus was the juvenile of Tuojiangosaurus.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul described the unique tail spike arrangement of Chungkingosaurus as a "pin-cushion array".
facts.quote: Paul described this kind of thagomizer as a "pin-cushion array".

facts.statement: The dorsal spikes of Chungkingosaurus are laterally compressed with sharp anterior and posterior edges.
facts.quote: Las espinas dorsales están comprimida lateralmente con los bordes anteriores y posteriores afilados.

facts.statement: Fossils of Chungkingosaurus were found near Chongqing, China, starting from 1977.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de Chungkingosaurus se encontraron cerca de Chongqing, China, desde 1977 en adelante.

facts.statement: The type species, Chungkingosaurus jiangbeiensis, was named and described by Dong Zhiming, Zhou Shiwu, and Zhang Yihong in 1983.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, Chungkingosaurus jiangbeiensis, fue nombrada y descrita por Dong Zhiming, Zhou Shiwu y Zhang Yihong en 1983.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton including the snout, front lower jaws, ten dorsal vertebrae, a pelvis with sacrum, twenty-three tail vertebrae, the lower end of a humerus, three metacarpals, both thigh bones and shin bones, and five rear plates.
facts.quote: Consiste en un esqueleto parcial, que contiene el hocico, la parte frontal de las mandíbulas inferiores, diez vértebras dorsales, una pelvis con sacro, una serie de veintitrés vértebras de la cola, el extremo inferior de un húmero, tres metacarpianos, ambos huesos de los muslos y espinillas y cinco placas traseras.

facts.statement: In 2014, Roman Ulansky named specimen CV 00205 as Chungkingosaurus giganticus and Chungkingosaurus magnus.
facts.quote: En 2014, Roman Ulansky nombró a CV 00205 Chungkingosaurus giganticus y CV 00205 como Chungkingosaurus magnus.

facts.statement: Peter Malcolm Galton and Kenneth Carpenter later identified both names as dubious and referred them to C. jiangbeiensis.
facts.quote: Peter Malcolm Galton y Kenneth Carpenter luego identificó a ambos como nomina dubia, refiriéndolos ambos a C. jiangbeiensis.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul suggested in 2010 that Chungkingosaurus was a juvenile of Tuojiangosaurus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, Gregory S. Paul en 2010 sugirió que Chungkingosaurus era el juvenil de Tuojiangosaurus.

facts.statement: Chungkingosaurus was placed within Stegosaurinae in 1983 by Dong et al.
facts.quote: Chungkingosaurus fue colocado en 1983 dentro de Stegosaurinae por Dong et al.

facts.statement: In 2008, Maidment et al. assigned Chungkingosaurus to the family Huayangosauridae.
facts.quote: En 2008, Maidment et al. lo asignaron a los Huayangosauridae.

facts.statement: The parent group of Chungkingosaurus is Stegosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Stegosauridae

facts.statement: Chungkingosaurus belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Chungkingosaurus lived during the Bathonian to Callovian stages, from 168.2 to 161.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Callovian (168.2 to 161.5 million years ago)
